title: Quantitative Analysis of Battery Cathode Nanoparticles using 4D-STEM and EELS
content: Chemo-mechanical coupling refers to chemical reactions or changes in composition that influence mechanical properties (such as strain, phase transformations, or defect formations) and, conversely, how mechanical forces affect chemical behavior (such as reduction reaction, diffusion, or ion insertions). This phenomenon significantly impacts the behaviors of cathode materials during electrochemical reactions. Conventional X-ray techniques such as X-ray diffraction (XRD) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) can provide a statistical analysis of crystal structure, chemical composition, and valence state of the elements [1]. However, due to the limitations of X-ray probe size, it is hard to achieve correlative analysis on a single nanoparticle with nanometer resolution. In scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), correlative imaging has been successfully shown to map structural and chemical response upon ion insertion using four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) and electron-energy loss spectroscopy (EELS). While 4D-STEM probes the lattice structure, including structure identification, orientation classification, and strain measurement with nanometer spatial resolution [2], core-loss EELS by calculating the L3/L2 area ratio enables tracking of the valence state of metal ions in cathode nanoparticles [3]. Chen et al. showed local structure heterogeneity of metal oxide cathode nanoparticles significantly influences ion insertion efficiency, leading to the formation of oriented phase domains [4].
